decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: "Add ... bookmarks"; round 1 client confirms "adding ... [is among] the everyday things I'd want."
decisions.note: The presented ability to add a bookmark conforms at the initial implementation-review stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: "Add, edit, delete"; round 1 client confirms "editing" and later says the existing features remain solid.
decisions.note: The recorded edit capability is conforming; no contrary field limitation is presented.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents "delete"; round 1 client includes "deleting" among the satisfactory everyday functions.
decisions.note: Deletion conforms at the initial implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents "archive, and restore"; round 1 client explicitly says "The archive-vs-delete distinction works the way I'd hope too."
decisions.note: Archive is presented as reversible and distinct from deletion, conforming to these requirements.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents "Search"; round 1 client lists "searching" among the everyday functions that work and later says the rest still holds up.
decisions.note: The recorded search decision is directionally conforming; the presentation does not assert a conflicting restriction.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents "tag filters" and bookmark editing; round 1 client explicitly confirms "tagging."
decisions.note: Assignment of tags is recorded as a conforming initial implementation decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: "tag filters"; round 1 client says the remaining shown functionality feels solid.
decisions.note: Filtering bookmarks by tag conforms at the initial implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents "sorting"; round 1 client includes "sorting" among the desired everyday functions.
decisions.note: The sorting decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents "collections"; round 1 client approves "keeping links in collections," but neither entry states whether collections dynamically save a search term plus included/excluded tags.
decisions.note: The collection semantics cannot be compared reliably with reference bundles. The client's approval does not clarify equivalence or explicitly accept a difference, so this remains unresolved at the initial implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents the completed add flow; round 1 client reports, "When I paste a URL, I have to type the title (and description) myself" and requests that the app "pulls in the page's title and description on its own."
decisions.note: The initial save flow omitted automatic metadata retrieval. The client surfaced the omission and requested the reference-aligned behavior during implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client reports that "the form even requires a title before it'll save" and supplies the desired behavior: "I drop in a link" and metadata is fetched automatically.
decisions.note: Requiring a title prevented URL-only saving. The client supplied the conforming URL-first behavior at the initial implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client: "There's no 'read later' / unread" and "I'd want to mark a bookmark as unread"; the maker's round 1 feature list offered favorite but no unread state.
decisions.note: The client identified and requested the missing unread/read-later capability.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client requests to "see just my unread ones in their own view" after observing that read-later/unread was absent.
decisions.note: The client requested the missing dedicated unread view during the initial implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client asks to "clear them once I've read them" while explaining the missing unread workflow.
decisions.note: The client requested the missing transition from unread to read.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker scopes automatic collection to "page title and description"; REF-BM-02 also requires favicon and preview image. Round 2 client praises the fetched title and says the raised issues are handled, without identifying the remaining metadata difference.
decisions.note: The revised implementation explicitly presents only two of the four required metadata types. The client does not express or correct the omitted favicon and preview-image collection.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: "Metadata remains editable before saving"; the prior implementation already presented editing, and the round 2 client confirms "I could still change it before saving" and that everything else still holds up.
decisions.note: The revised metadata remains editable before saving, while the retained edit capability covers subsequent editing; this is conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: "Title is no longer required; the domain is used as a fallback"; round 2 client confirms the effortless URL-save flow is what was wanted.
decisions.note: The revised flow permits saving from the URL without requiring a manually entered title.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: "New bookmarks default to unread"; round 2 client confirms "new links start as unread."
decisions.note: The revised implementation supplies an unread/read-later state.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: "Added a dedicated Unread view with a live count"; round 2 client confirms "there's an Unread view with a running count."
decisions.note: The revised dedicated unread view conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: "Each card now has a one-click Read/Unread toggle"; round 2 client confirms "I can flip something to read (or back) in one tap."
decisions.note: The toggle provides conforming read and unread transitions in the revised implementation.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: "Unread status is preserved when editing and stored locally"; round 2 client says the read-later behavior works as pictured.
decisions.note: Preserving the state through editing is consistent with the required unread workflow.
